finding.claim: The /preview endpoint fetches a fully attacker-supplied URL with no allowlist, scheme check, or IP restriction. Redirects are followed by default. Part of the response body (status and the first 500 characters) is returned to the caller, so this is full-read SSRF. An attacker can reach cloud metadata (169.254.169.254), loopback, and RFC-1918 services. Severity: HIGH. No authentication is present on the route.
finding.sink: requests.get(target, timeout=5) (app.py:16); response returned via jsonify at app.py:17

trace.note: Public Flask route /preview, no auth decorator
requests.get(target, timeout=5), with no validation between source and sink; redirects followed by default
status code and resp.text[:500] returned to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: No host allowlist, no scheme restriction, no IP/CIDR blocking, no allow_redirects=False, and no authentication. The ALLOWED_HOSTS check is applied only in /partner, not here. Repro: GET /preview?url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/

verdict.reason: app.py:15 takes the `url` query parameter and app.py:16 passes it straight to requests.get() with no validation, and app.py:17 returns the status and the first 500 characters of the body; the ALLOWED_HOSTS check at app.py:23-25 exists only in /partner, and app.py has no auth decorator or middleware.
